source: v104 measured contact-point motion: in s02 the receiver foot moves with the incoming ball and a real second foot shot follows; in s04 the foot moves against a slow ball, reverses it, and the B6 chain dies. Test whether sender action timing can align arrival with a better receiver gait phase without changing ball physics or actor weights.
baseline_reproduction_gate: Entry 0 must reproduce v103 candidate 04 local s02 B6 first-foot frame within 2 of 66 and second-foot frame within 2 of 83, with six-body safety and no intervening nonfoot collision. Otherwise course invalid.
two_scene_gate: Both scenes must be six-body safe, clean source/receiver foot transfer, dynamic incoming speed >=0.30 m/s, no robot collision, and receiver own second foot >=0.20 s after first touch, outgoing speed >=2.0 m/s, with no intervening nonfoot ball contact.
selection: Among 2/2 passing timings choose smallest entry frame, then highest minimum second-foot outgoing speed. No winner from failed rows. A consumed timing success is only an unqualified coordination teacher, not a learned player, full goal, or promotional video.
next_if_failed: Use 500 Hz foot/contact state to train receiver-phase prediction and a continuous motor policy; do not keep widening static timing grid on the same consumed scenes.
